subject: Proposed DPA redlines — processor accountability & model-output rights
messages:
From: Eliza Kim <eliza@lifeline.health>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Lifeline Health Legal <legal@lifeline.health>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed DPA redlines — runtime telemetry & model output rights

Hi Elliot —

Thanks for the demo last week. Our legal team attached a redline of Redwood's standard DPA and a short security questionnaire. Two items are blocking procurement for our Q4 pilot:

1) Model output rights: Lifeline needs an explicit clause that grants us ownership (or an exclusive license) of model outputs generated from our data and prompts during our usage period. This is critical for downstream clinical workflows we are integrating.

2) Runtime telemetry & telemetry retention: we require retention of telemetry (request/response pairs and runtime logs) for 90 days and the ability to export them on demand. We also need assurance that telemetry will not be used to train models beyond the duration of the agreement.

3) Subprocessors: please provide an allowlist of subprocessors (cloud infra, monitoring, analytics) and commit to notify us within 30 days of any additions.

We appreciate small edits but these are dealbreakers for our InfoSec/procurement timelines. Can you route this to product + security for a quick read and get back with a counterproposal by next Tue?

Attachments: lifeline_dpa_redline_v1.pdf, lifeline_security_questionnaire.xlsx

Best,
Eliza
Legal Ops — Lifeline Health

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposed DPA redlines — please advise (runtime telemetry & output rights)

Folks — forwarding Lifeline's redline. TL;DR: they want ownership/exclusive license to model outputs, 90d telemetry retention with exportability, no-training guarantees, and an explicit subprocessor allowlist + 30-day notice. Q4 pilot target, procurement is pushing.

Key product/security implications I see:
- "Ownership" of outputs is a broad ask; we need product/legal to propose targeted language that protects IP and our service model.
- 90d telemetry retention increases storage and could conflict with our minimization policies — need security input on what telemetry can look like (hashed vs raw).
- Subprocessor allowlist: we already publish a list, but they want a contractual allowlist and 30d notification.

Questions for you:
1) Marissa — can Product accept a contractual output license (time-limited & use-limited) instead of full assignment? What are the minimum invariants (metadata we must keep, ability to use outputs for debugging/quality)?
2) Olga — Security: is 90d reasonable if we pseudonymize or redact prompts? What telemetry can we agree to without exposing raw prompts? Also flagged: KMS/HSM requirements?
3) Ben — any operational constraints (cost, infra) if we change default retention or provide export tooling?

Attached Lifeline's files. For meeting rhythm, can we aim to sync tomorrow EOD and I'll draft a counterproposal to send early next week?

---- Forwarded message ----
%FROM%

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed DPA redlines — product input on output rights & runtime

Elliot / team — thanks for flagging. My read (product):

- Ownership vs license: We should not assign ownership of model outputs. Proposed approach: grant Lifeline a "limited, perpetual (or duration-based) license" to use outputs for their internal business purposes and integrations created during the contract term. Explicitly prohibit downstream training on Redwood models. That preserves our ability to operate and improve the service (we can retain anonymized metrics), while giving the customer what they need for clinical workflows.

- Telemetry retention: default 30d is our current offering. Lifeline's 90d ask is material. We can offer a configurable retention tier: 30d default; 90d as a paid add-on for pilot customers, with clear caps and export tooling. That buys them time for integration while giving us a commercial lever.

- Exportability / UI: we'll need to add a one-click export job in Console (CSV/ndjson) and an S3 export endpoint. That will take ~2 sprints to ship (plus security review).

- No-training clause: we can accept a strong no-training clause (no use of customer prompts/outputs to train models) but we must reserve the right to use aggregated, non-identifiable metrics for system health and safety. Suggest language to be vetted by legal.

If we follow this path, here's the ask for contracting: we want Lifeline to accept the license model and the paid 90d retention add-on. If they insist on ownership, that's a product showstopper.

I'll draft counter-language today. Ben, estimates on infra/cost for 90d retention and export? Olga, can you confirm security constraints for export and the pseudonymization approaches?

-Marissa
Senior PM, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed DPA redlines — security signoff conditions

Team — security perspective below. High level: we can sign off conditionally, but several technical and contractual guards are required.

1) Telemetry content: we cannot provide raw request text and response content in telemetry that is retained for long periods unless the customer accepts the data residency and protection profile. Options:
   - Provide hashed/pseudonymized prompt hashes + response meta for 90d retention.
   - Allow full request/response export only on-demand with strict S3 encryption + audit trail and a signed SOW for extended retention.

2) No-training / model use: we can contractually agree to no-training on customer-provided prompts/outputs. Security will require automated controls to mark and exclude customer data from training pipelines (labeling + ACL) and quarterly attestations. This is enforceable but requires changes to pipelines and monitoring.

3) KMS & encryption: for exported telemetry and any long-retained logs, customer-managed keys (BYOK) via KMS is preferred. If customer cannot provide BYOK, we will store logs encrypted with our keys and provide access controls and audit logs.

4) Subprocessors: we will provide the current subprocessor list. Contractually commit to notify customers 30 days prior to onboarding a new subprocessor, with right to terminate for material changes. Any monitoring/analytics vendors that process raw content must be explicitly named or excluded.

5) On-prem / private deployment: if Lifeline requires full control over telemetry retention or ownership, recommend Private or Dedicated deployment (different commercial terms + SOW).

Attachments: security_evidence_checklist.pdf

If product accepts the license + paid retention tier approach, security can agree to a redline that: a) accepts 90d as paid tier, b) requires export controls and pseudonymization by default, and c) requires BYOK for certain export retention scenarios.

-Olga
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Kim <eliza@lifeline.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lifeline Health Legal <legal@lifeline.health>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redlines — draft counterproposal and signoff path

Eliza — thanks for the detailed redline and the checklist. We've reviewed internally (Product + Security + Ops) and can propose the following counterpoints for Lifeline's review:

1) Model outputs: Redwood cannot assign ownership of generated outputs. We propose a limited, perpetual license to use outputs produced during contract term for Lifeline's internal business purposes, explicitly prohibiting customer-provided materials from being used to train Redwood models. This matches the needs you described while protecting Redwood's service and IP.

2) Telemetry retention: default telemetry retention remains 30 days. We can offer a 90-day retention add-on (commercial, one-time setup + monthly storage fee) that includes: pseudonymized logs by default, an on-demand full-export capability to an encrypted S3 bucket (BYOK preferred), and an audit trail of exports. Full raw-export requires an SOW and additional security attestation.

3) Subprocessors & notice: we'll provide the current subprocessor list in the contract; Redwood will give 30 days' notice before adding new subprocessors and will allow Lifeline contractual termination rights for material changes.

Next steps: attached is our draft counterproposal (redwood_counterproposal_v1.pdf). If Lifeline is OK on the license + paid retention tier model, Security is prepared to sign off on the redline language subject to BYOK/export controls and pipeline exclusions for training.

Can we schedule a short call tomorrow to finalize language? Also sending a DocuSign placeholder link to accelerate execution after legal rounds: https://www.docusign.com/link/placeholder-LFN-3721-counter

Thanks —
Elliot
Business Development (Sales) — Redwood Inference
